newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto-Dominion, National Bank Q2 profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Toronto-Dominion, National Bank Q2 profits rise.

text.p: Toronto-Dominion Bank and National Bank of Canada said on Thursday they posted higher second-quarter profits, but they fell short of their record first-quarter performances.

Toronto-Dominion, Canada's fifth largest bank, earned C$240 million ($173 million) or C76 cents a share (55 cents a share) in the period ended April 30, up from C$220 million ($158 million) or C69 cents (50 cents) a share in the year ago period.
But the earnings were down from its record first-quarter net profit of C$256 million ($184 million) or C83 cents (60 cents) a share.

Second-quarter earnings at sixth-ranked National Bank rose to C$80 million ($57 million) or C44 cents (32 cents) a share from year earlier C$71 million ($51 million) or C39 cents (28 cents) a share in the year ago period.
But Montreal-based National Bank's earnings were also down from its first-quarter profit of C$83.8 million ($60.3 million) or C46 cents (33 cents) a share.
National Bank's second-quarter profit bested analysts' expectations of C43 cents (31 cents) a share.

Analysts had forecast Toronto-Dominion earnings per share of C84 cents (61 cents). The bank said its earnings would have been C86 cents (62 cents) a share if not for a C$29 million ($21 million) or 10 cent (7 cent) a share charge for its acquisition of Australian discount broker Pont Securities Ltd.

Shares of both banks fell on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday, in concert with an overall slide in North American stocks. Toronto-Dominion declined C55 cents to $41.40 and National Bank slid C45 cents to $16.05.

"Even though the bank earnings are very healthy, if they are in line with analysts' expectations it's already been priced into the stock," said Katherine Beattie, technical analyst at economics firm MMS International.
Both banks said their earnings rose due to a strengthening Canadian economy and rising loan demand.

Toronto-Dominion said its net impaired loans declined to C$367 million ($265 million) in the second quarter from $514 million ($371 million) at the end of the first quarter and from $395 million ($285 million) a year ago.
Its provision for credit losses fell to C$40 million ($29 million) from C$42 million ($30 million) in the year ago period, but was unchanged from the first quarter.

National Bank said its second-quarter provision for loan losses rose to C$56.3 million ($41 million) from C$43.8 million ($32 million) a year earlier. But the bank said its estimated loan losses for full-year fiscal 1997 were C$225 million ($163 million), compared to C$235 million ($170 million) in 1996.
